north_star: Produce a frozen and falsifiable 2026 territorial probabilistic forecast whose national centre, territorial geography and uncertainty are separately validated before any seat probability is promoted.

rolling_origin_model_selection.selection_metric: equal-weight mean party-share RMSE across folds

structural_point_seat_reference.interpretation: Credible structural centre/reference only; its v2 quantiles and first-party probabilities are NOT promoted as calibrated 2026 probabilities.

current_national_2026_point.reason: Current public evidence collected so far contains useful turnout, revealed-preference and candidate/dynamics signals but no defensible representative party vote-intention shares.

territorial_center_v3.formula: national_2026 + 0.5*(territory_2021-national_2021), followed only when necessary by positive raking to recover the exact national target
territorial_center_v3.invariant: If national_2026 equals national_2021, the formula is exactly the validated HALF_SHRINK centre.

conditional_territorial_uncertainty_v3.scope: Retrospective territorial residuals conditional on realized target national strength, separating geography error from national-shock error.
conditional_territorial_uncertainty_v3.interpretation: This calibrates only the conditional geography component; it is not total prospective forecast error.

national_uncertainty_v3.reason: The new national point model must first be defined; its uncertainty then needs comparable historical calibration or an explicitly conservative frozen alternative.

legal_allocator_2026.policy: reuse existing fail-closed allocator; do not modify legal mechanics merely because the statistical centre changed

old_Fminus1_uncertainty_around_new_half_.reason: It was calibrated for the previous persistence-centred architecture and produces implausibly broad v2 seat intervals when transplanted around the new centre.

promotion_rule: PROMOTED only after current national point + national uncertainty + conditional territorial residual calibration + correlation/resampling rule + rolling-origin interval coverage + >=50000 legally valid 395-seat simulations all pass.
